title: Pulse Console visual + interaction upgrade

visual: Full driver-console visual pass after lifecycle controls are simplified
Stronger ride hierarchy, cleaner spacing, fewer glass panels and internal labels
Use route/fare/status/next action as the dominant information
Retain Pulse night visual identity and current Leaflet map functionality
Make incoming request, Scheduled, pickup, active trip, and completion states visually distinct
Remove TEST/debug chrome from the normal live driving surface
Remove opportunity/event card from the primary driving surface; event intelligence remains a secondary information lane
Make Uber trip-mirroring controls visually secondary whenever a Pulse rider request/ride is active
interaction: Guard request and ride lifecycle buttons against rapid repeat taps while a transition is in flight
Remove ambiguous DUE labels that have no numeric/time context
Normalize Accept ride / Route to pickup labels into a single clear next action
Do not change request writer, fare writer, rider lifecycle writer, or Uber mirror data capture
followOn: End Shift direct-finish cleanup after live server end-shift function is captured/verified
Background refresh/polling hardening after current production refresh function is captured/verified
MapLibre remains optional future map visual upgrade rather than a blocker

acceptance: Console looks like a purpose-built driver app rather than an admin dashboard
Incoming request, Scheduled, active Pulse ride, and Uber mirror mode are immediately distinguishable
Opportunity/test/debug cards do not occupy the primary live-driving surface
Fare remains prominent on incoming requests and Scheduled rides
One dominant next action is presented for rider lifecycle states
Rapid repeat taps are temporarily blocked client-side
Uber mirror controls no longer dominate while a Pulse rider request/ride is active
No regression in QR, fare, Inbox, Scheduled, map, shift, Uber mirroring, or rider lifecycle
